notes: The runner, report, and dashboard all resolve the tier through routing.tier_from_nouls so they cannot disagree. produces_analysis (v2.1) was tested and removed: it did not generalise.

tier_definitions.T0: A capable local model of roughly 12B parameters or less. Bounded rewriting, extraction, formatting, simple code, and clear single-step tasks with limited context.
tier_definitions.T1: An inexpensive hosted general model. Needs more context, constraints, or polish than a small local model handles dependably, but no genuine multi-step reasoning.
tier_definitions.T2: A high-capability, cost-efficient cloud model. Genuine multi-step synthesis, professional analysis, repository work, tool use, or moderately complex judgment.
tier_definitions.T3: A premium frontier or deliberate-reasoning model. Deep ambiguity, conflicting evidence, high-stakes judgment, long-horizon planning, or complex cross-system work.

single_step.instructions: This request can be completed reliably as a single bounded step with limited context: a short rewrite, formatting change, extraction, classification of short items, or a simple factual or computational answer.

multistep.instructions: Reaching a reliable, professional result requires genuine multi-step reasoning, analysis, or synthesis, rather than merely rewriting, condensing, reformatting, or applying one rule.

deep.instructions: The request involves deep ambiguity, conflicting or incomplete evidence, high-stakes judgment, long-horizon planning, or complex cross-system work, where a weaker model's errors would be costly.

context.instructions: Answering reliably requires integrating a large or complex body of context or evidence, such as many sources, long documents, or cross-system state.

mapping: single_step >= s and context < c  -> T0

tuning.trained_on: development split, grouped CV by template

boundary_rules: Choose the minimum tier, not the best possible answer.
Judge only the intrinsic capability the request needs; ignore vendor, price, and the requester's organization.
Volume, length, or the number of items does NOT raise the tier: processing more items is code's job. A 300-item classification needs no more capability than a 15-item one.
Mentioning tools or attachments does not raise the tier by itself; the required judgment does.
T1 vs T2 is the decisive boundary: T1 transforms provided content (rewrite, condense, adapt, reformat, classify); T2 produces new analysis, design, or judgement.
Any deep ambiguity, conflicting evidence, high stakes, long horizon, or cross-system integration is T3.

history.change: Replaced one holistic 4-way Choice with four atomic Nouls combined in code.
Added a produces_analysis Noul with true/false anchors to sharpen T1 vs T2.

Removed produces_analysis. On the blind test the 5-feature rule scored 68.9% vs 72.2% for the 4-feature rule; the signal did not generalise. Also fixed duplicated mapping logic so runner/report/dashboard agree.

audit_findings.note: Categories are tier-mixed. Boundary noise is concentrated at T1/T2. Merging T1/T2 raises accuracy from ~72% to ~83%, i.e. T0, {T1,T2} and T3 are separable from a prompt but T1 vs T2 is not.
